item.title: DataFrame caching on serverless compute is now in Public Preview
item.description: DataFrame caching on serverless compute is now in Public Preview. You can cache a DataFrame with df.cache() or df.persist() on serverless compute to reuse an expensive result for the rest of your session. Caching requires serverless environment version 5 or above, Databricks Connect for Python 18.1.8 or above, or Databricks Connect for Scala 18.1.5 or above. The preview is enabled by default for most workspaces. Workspace admins can disable it from the Previews page. See Cache DataFrames on serverless compute.

item.title: Google Analytics Aggregated connector is available in Beta
item.description:
The managed Google Analytics Aggregated connector is now available in Lakeflow Connect in Beta. Workspace admins can control access to this feature from the Previews page.

Use the connector to ingest aggregated Google Analytics 4 report data, such as user activity, acquisition, engagement, monetization, demographics, and tech reports, into Databricks. You can also define custom reports with your own dimensions, metrics, and aggregation level. The connector supports incremental ingestion and both service account and OAuth user-to-machine (U2M) authentication.

item.title: Files API 3.0 for Unity Catalog volumes is now in Beta
item.description:
Files API 3.0 is in Beta and introduces two new capabilities:

  • Multipart uploads: Upload files larger than 5 GB to Unity Catalog volumes.
  • Conditional operations: Upload, download, and delete files based on their current version to prevent unintended changes.

For more information, see What is Files API?.

item.title: Box Audit Logs managed ingestion connector (Beta)
item.description: The Box Audit Logs connector in Lakeflow Connect is now available in Beta. Use the connector to ingest enterprise audit events from Box into Databricks. See Box Audit Logs connector.

item.title: Genie One enhancements
item.description:
• Conversation outline: Use the conversation outline along the left edge of Genie One conversations to jump between your messages. Hover over a tick in the outline to preview a message and the start of its response. See Navigate a long conversation.
  • Upload skills (Public Preview): You can now click Upload skills to upload your existing skill files and folders to your skills folder in the workspace. See Upload a skill.
  • Snippets from external tool queries (Public Preview): Genie Ontology now also extracts snippets from queries that external tools, such as dbt, run on Databricks. These runs appear in query history alongside queries that you run in Databricks. See Genie Ontology.
  • Remembered sign-in email in the Genie mobile app (Public Preview): The Genie mobile app now remembers the email address of the last user who signed in and prefills it at the next sign-in. See Use Genie on mobile.

item.title: Dashboard enhancements
item.description:
• Private bookmarks: Dashboard viewers can now save filter combinations as private bookmarks to return to later. Private bookmarks are visible only to the user who creates them. See Save a private bookmark.
  • Bulk import from Power BI and Tableau: Genie Code can now import up to 100 Power BI or Tableau files at a time as AI/BI dashboards and metric views. See Import multiple files in bulk.
  • Field picker tooltips: Hovering over a field or measure name in the field picker now shows its full name in a tooltip.
  • Layered combo charts: Authors can now build combo charts from separate chart layers. See Combo chart.
  • Custom waterfall totals: Authors can now customize totals on waterfall charts. See Waterfall chart.
  • Sankey label improvements: Labels on Sankey diagrams now overlap less.

item.title: Serverless job environments from pyproject.toml (Beta)
item.description: Serverless notebook and Python script tasks can use a pyproject.toml file to configure their job environment. Configure the project environment in the Jobs UI, the Jobs API, or a bundle. Workspace admins can enable Project-Scoped Shared Compute on the Previews page. See Configure a project environment with pyproject.toml.

item.title: Shared Serverless for Asset Bundles (Beta)
item.description: With Shared Serverless for Asset Bundles, notebooks and files in the same bundle can share serverless compute and an environment defined in the bundle-root pyproject.toml file. Workspace admins can enable Project-Scoped Shared Compute on the Previews page. See Shared Serverless for Asset Bundles.

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID connector is available in Beta
item.description:
The managed Microsoft Entra ID connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect.

Use the connector to ingest Microsoft Entra ID users, groups, applications, service principals, directory roles, identity configuration, and audit and sign-in logs into Databricks. The connector uses OAuth machine-to-machine authentication and supports incremental ingestion for audit and sign-in logs.

item.title: Genie Code tasks in Lakeflow Jobs are available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled starting in November 2026
item.description:
Starting in November 2026, Genie Code tasks in Lakeflow Jobs are available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled.

A Genie Code task runs your prompt autonomously as part of a job. It can read upstream task outputs and call tools as needed, and it returns a link to the resulting Genie Code chat with its response.

See Genie Code task for jobs.

item.title: Lakebase Insights moves to per-project settings, with on-demand runs (Beta)
item.description:
Lakebase Insights now diagnoses issues using telemetry from the system.lakebase system tables and recommends next steps. The Lakebase Insights workspace preview enables automatic telemetry capture. Users with CAN MANAGE can configure Insights directly in each project's Settings, without creating an observability configuration.

This preview was previously named Lakebase Advanced Postgres Telemetry. Workspaces that used Insights before already have it enabled. To set up Insights:

  • If the preview isn't already enabled, ask a workspace admin to enable Lakebase Insights from the Previews page. Insights needs telemetry in system.lakebase to analyze a project, so enabling the Insights preview also enables Lakebase Observability in System Tables if it isn't already enabled. Workspace admins can enable the observability preview separately to capture telemetry without Insights.
  • To schedule Insights runs for a project, you need CAN MANAGE on that project. Enable Insights and set its analysis frequency in Settings.
  • You can run Insights on demand at any time, with or without a schedule.

If you scheduled Insights through an observability configuration, those jobs have stopped. Their schedules do not carry over. Those configurations no longer write telemetry to their Unity Catalog destinations, so their dashboards retain historical data but receive no new data.

To continue receiving scheduled insights, enable Insights and set an analysis frequency in each project's Settings. Each project runs separately, and each run uses compute and model tokens, so choose which projects to analyze and how often. Insights remains in Beta. See Detect issues with Insights.

item.title: Databricks Runtime 19: October 19, 2026
item.description:
Behavioral changes

  • Spark Connect DataFrame execution metrics now hide internal operators and metrics associated with row filters and column masks. This protects information about policy execution when inspecting df.executionInfo.metrics, including its text representation. The boundary of the protected portion of the plan and its own metrics remain visible. Query results are unchanged. Notebooks or tools that depend on detailed metrics inside protected subplans may need to be updated.

item.title: Saving an unchanged job no longer adds rows to the jobs system tables
item.description: Saving a job without changing its settings no longer adds rows to system.lakeflow.jobs or system.lakeflow.job_tasks, and change_time stays at the last change. This applies to saves from the UI, the Jobs API, and Declarative Automation Bundles. See Jobs table schema.

item.title: Filter data per end user with OAuth custom identity claims
item.description:
You can now add a custom identity claim to a service principal's OAuth token and filter rows by it in a dynamic view or ABAC policy. Serve many end users through one service principal while each sees only their own data.

See Filter data per end user with OAuth custom identity claims.

item.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is scheduled for retirement

item.title: Asynchronous processing with transformWithState is now generally available
item.description: Asynchronous processing for the Python row-based transformWithState API is now generally available. Run state operations and user logic concurrently for higher throughput with only minor code changes. See Asynchronous processing with transformWithState.

item.title: File upload in Genie One and Genie Agents will soon be available by default for compliance security profile workspaces with supported compliance standards
item.description:
Starting November 15, 2026, file upload in Genie One and Genie Agents will be available by default for workspaces that have the compliance security profile enabled, if the workspace's compliance standard supports file upload. You can upload files to a conversation and analyze them in natural language alongside your other data.

Workspaces with a compliance standard that doesn't support file upload yet can't use it. To check whether your standard supports file upload, open its page from the list of supported compliance standards and see the feature availability table.

See Upload a file and Upload a file to a Genie Agent.

item.title: Delegate budget access with access control lists (ACLs)
item.description: Budgets now support access control lists (ACLs). Account and workspace admins can grant the Budget Manager or Budget Viewer role to users, groups, or Databricks service principals, delegating who can view and manage a budget. See Manage budget permissions.

item.title: TypeSafe AI Jev 1.14.0 is now available on Unity Gateway
item.description: TypeSafe AI Jev 1.14.0 is now available on Unity Gateway. TypeSafe AI hosts it, and an account admin must enable the TypeSafe AI Models preview. TypeSafe's terms govern its use.

item.title: Delegate access to Genie budgets
item.description: Budgets used to manage Genie costs now support access control lists (ACLs). Account admins and workspace admins can grant the Budget Manager or Budget Viewer role to specific users, groups, or Databricks service principals, delegating who can view and manage each budget. See Manage budget permissions and Manage budgets and cost controls for Genie.

item.title: File upload in Genie One and Genie Agents is now generally available
item.description:
File upload in Genie One and Genie Agents is now generally available, so workspace admins no longer need to turn on a preview. Upload files to a conversation and analyze them in natural language alongside your other data. For supported file types and limits, see Upload a file and Upload a file to a Genie Agent.

File upload in Genie One isn't supported for users who have only consumer access.

item.title: Consumer access to query Unity Gateway services is generally available
item.description:
Users with the consumer access entitlement no longer need an account admin to enable the "Consumer access to Unity Gateway" preview to query the model services and model provider services shared with them, or to use Unity Gateway coding agent features. See Consumer access capabilities.

This change can increase model traffic from consumer access users, including traffic to external providers. To control this traffic, account admins can set budgets and rate limits, or disable direct model access, for consumer access users. See Manage budgets for Unity Gateway, Apply rate limits to model and MCP services, and Manage entitlements.

item.title: Genie Agents enhancements
item.description:
• Flash (Beta): Agent mode now offers Flash, an option that prioritizes response speed over depth. Flash is most efficient on simpler, everyday tasks. See Flash.
  • Agent mode model upgrade: Agent mode now uses upgraded models that better handle long context and respond faster. See Agent mode.

item.title: Genie One enhancements
item.description:
• Collaborative document editing: People you share a Genie One document with can now edit it if they have CAN EDIT permission. See Share a document.
  • Group memberships in user info: When Genie One retrieves a user's information, it now also returns the user's group memberships. You can use workspace instructions and table descriptions to tailor how Genie One responds to members of specific groups.
  • Reuse context from past investigations: When you ask a question similar to one you asked before, Genie One can now use the context from the earlier investigation to answer faster. See Recall past conversations.
  • Share skills with Unity Gateway (Beta): You can now publish Genie One skills to a Unity Catalog schema and share them with your team. Unity Gateway governs shared skills, so teammates can discover and install existing skills from one central location instead of keeping copies in sync. See Share a skill with your team.

item.title: Dashboard enhancements and bug fixes
item.description:
• Lakehouse Real-Time warehouse support (Beta): AI/BI dashboards now work with Lakehouse Real-Time SQL warehouses. See Use Lakehouse Real-Time with AI/BI dashboards.
  • Dashboard Insights (Beta): Viewers can now have Genie analyze the charts on a published dashboard page and summarize notable findings, such as trends and outliers, as insight cards. See Dashboard Insights.
  • Import Power BI .tmdl files: Authors can now upload Power BI .tmdl files to create metric views with the /importBI Genie Code skill. See Import one file at a time.
  • Pivot table drill-down: Viewers can now drill down through the row and column hierarchy of a pivot table one level at a time. See Drill down in pivot tables.
  • Theme fonts for rich text titles: Rich text widget titles and descriptions now inherit the dashboard theme's font styles. See Customize colors and fonts.
  • Pivot table null header fix: Pivot tables now show NULL values and the text null as separate headers instead of merging them into one.
  • Cross-dataset measure export fix: Exported cross-dataset measures now use the measure name as the column header.
  • Decimal precision fix: Visualizations that Genie generates now respect decimal precision.

item.title: Consumer access to query Unity Gateway services is generally available
item.description:

To control this traffic, account admins can set budgets and rate limits, or disable direct model access, for consumer access users. See Manage budgets for Unity Gateway, Apply rate limits to model and MCP services, and Manage entitlements.

item.title: Redesigned MLflow Logs tab for AI Runtime runs
item.description: The MLflow run page Logs tab for AI Runtime runs now supports searching and filtering logs by node, level, and time range, following a running workload as new output arrives, and downloading logs. For new runs, it replaces the log files previously stored on the run's Artifacts tab, which are deprecated. Logs are available for 60 days. Logs for existing runs remain on the Artifacts tab. See View logs in the MLflow Logs tab.

item.title: Databricks AI Runtime SDK replaces serverless_gpu
item.description:
Starting in GPU environment version 6, the Databricks AI Runtime SDK (databricks-sdk-air) replaces the deprecated serverless_gpu package. It provides the @distributed and ray_init APIs and the databricks.air.data utilities under the databricks.air namespace. The gpus and gpu_type arguments are renamed to num_accelerators and accelerator_type. The old names still work in databricks.air but emit a FutureWarning, and support will end in version 7.

Serverless GPU environment version 6 includes both packages. Version 6 is the last version that includes serverless_gpu. Versions 5 and below continue to use it. See Migrate from serverless_gpu.

item.title: Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent are now legacy
item.description: Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent are now legacy offerings. For new agents written in code, Databricks recommends the Agent Bricks CLI. To build agents without code, use Genie Agents. See Legacy agent offerings.

item.title: Use OpenJev as the evaluator for LLM-as-a-judge service policies (Beta)
item.description: You can now select OpenJev (Qwen3.5 4B) as the evaluator model service of a custom LLM-as-a-judge service policy. OpenJev classifies content without generating output tokens, so it typically responds faster than a chat evaluator. See Use OpenJev as the evaluator.

item.title: Use request tags in Unity Gateway service policies (Beta)
item.description: Custom service policies in Unity Gateway can now check caller-supplied request tags, such as requiring a tag before a model request or MCP tool call proceeds. See Request tags.

item.title: Unity Gateway supports Amazon Bedrock Mantle
item.description: You can now access Amazon Bedrock Mantle models through Unity Gateway model provider services, with Unity Catalog permissions, rate limits, budgets, and inference tables. See Model providers external to Databricks.

item.description: Custom service policies in Unity Gateway can now check caller-supplied request tags, such as requiring a tag before a model request or MCP tool call proceeds. See Request tags.

item.title: Genie Agents enhancements and bug fixes
item.description:
• Connect to external tools (Beta): A Genie Agent can now search and take actions in external tools like Google Drive and Microsoft 365 through MCP connectors. See Connect a Genie Agent to external tools and sources.
  • Automatic content search on attached volumes (Beta): When you attach a volume to a Genie Agent, Databricks now automatically enables content search for it. See How content search works.
  • Automatic volume sync (Beta): Content search now stays in sync with attached volumes automatically. When you add, change, or remove files, Databricks updates the index without any manual step. See How content search works.
  • Volumes from restricted catalogs (Beta): You can now attach a volume as a source for a Genie Agent even when the volume's catalog isn't accessible from the agent's workspace by default, such as a catalog that is bound to specific workspaces. See Attach volumes to a Genie Agent.
  • File upload fix: Fixed a bug where uploading a file to a Genie Agent through Genie One created duplicate conversations.
  • Deletion warning for sources and instructions: Deleting sources or instructions from a Genie Agent now asks you to confirm to prevent accidental deletions.
  • Column display name fix: Fixed a bug where Genie Code did not update column display names in a Genie Agent.

item.title: The Discover page and domains are now GA
item.description: The Discover page and domains are now generally available. Discover is a curated browsing experience that helps users find assets across Databricks without requiring deep knowledge of catalog hierarchies. Use domains and subdomains to organize assets such as tables, dashboards, notebooks, and Genie Agents by business area, highlight key assets with custom curation, and explore AI-recommended assets.

item.title: Enforce partner guardrails with external service policies (Beta)
item.description: You can now enforce a third-party guardrail on Unity Gateway traffic. An external service policy sends request and response content to your guardrail vendor and blocks the call when the vendor denies it, with no changes to your applications. See Enforce a partner guardrail with an external service policy.
